PullRequest.Title: chat: Show MCP server error details in customizations
PullRequest.Body:
Part of #333542.

## Summary

- Show existing native connection errors and agent-host `state.error.message` beneath installed MCP server names in Customizations home and search. The active session remains authoritative for matched rows.
- Replace the normal description only while errored, with a localized fallback for missing details. Render runtime messages as plain text with full wrapping, preserved newlines, and padding.
- Use dynamic virtual-list measurements and matching section allocation so errors can grow and shrink without clipping. Healthy rows retain their compact geometry.
- Remove the redundant trailing error icon. Keep the Error badge, enable switch, and more-actions menu, with Show Output routed through the existing native or current-session host diagnostics.
- Keep full managed hovers and accessible row labels fresh across message updates, recovery, disablement, session switches, and row recycling. Preserve action-button identity and focus.

This is iteration 01 only: no startup-progress, authentication-explanation, policy-diagnostic, history/logging, or SDK/AHP contract changes. Marketplace cards are unchanged.

## Testing

- `npm run compile-client` — passed, including client compilation with zero errors.
- `node build/hygiene.ts` with the four changed file paths — passed; the normal pre-commit hook also ran hygiene successfully on all four staged files.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/mcpListWidget.test.ts` — 69 passing, rerun against compile output.
- `npm run typecheck-client` and targeted ESLint — passed during final implementation validation.
- Targeted stylelint — passed, with existing design-token suggestions only.
- Production Component Explorer validation: 16 captures across native/host home and search, wide/narrow layouts, light/dark/high-contrast themes, and unchanged Sign In. DOM checks verify complete error text and final characters, no overlap or horizontal overflow, no trailing error icon/empty slot, and intact badge/switch/menu controls.
- Regression tests cover native and host-authoritative menu output routing, current-session binding, missing/multiline/long errors, message-only changes, recovery/disablement, dynamic resize, collapsed/offscreen rows, recycling, scroll anchors, and remaining-button focus/click stability.

Runtime data in the UI validation is synthetic. Live MCP/OAuth and spoken screen-reader output were not exercised.

## Screenshot

Production Customizations UI with synthetic MCP fixture data: the complete error wraps beneath the server name, with additional spacing and no trailing error icon. Show Output remains available from the menu.

![MCP error shown in full beneath the server name, retaining the Error badge, toggle, and menu without the trailing X](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b977c09b-a145-4264-9ee9-e34c39a87082)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The unbounded upstream sources, direct full-text assignment, no-clipping CSS, and synchronous dynamic-height measurement are all directly traced. Payload prevalence and exact duration vary, which limits severity to medium.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Error-message bytes, DOM text/ARIA/hover state, and browser text wrapping and row-height calculation
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows linearly with the unbounded error string and its wrapped line count. The full value is assigned to the row, hover, and ARIA label; dynamic-height measurement then synchronously computes the potentially enormous wrapped height, and width changes repeat wrapping.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Long UI-thread stalls, excessive memory/layout work, and an extremely tall Customizations scroll surface for verbose server failures.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Errored servers remained fixed-height rows showing a compact status indication; arbitrary error payload text was not inserted into or measured by the Customizations list.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The renderer now assigns the complete raw error message to textContent and the accompanying CSS uses pre-wrap, overflow-wrap:anywhere, and visible overflow, so no display or measurement bound remains.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 383 newly assigns the unbounded error string to the visible description; before this PR error payloads were not rendered in the row.
Findings.Title: Bound error text before laying it out inline
Findings.Impact: Opening Customizations after an HTTP MCP endpoint returns a large error body, or after an SDK reports verbose startup diagnostics, can freeze or severely jank the editor while that full payload is wrapped and measured.
Findings.Evidence: The new assignment at line 383 uses the complete value returned by getMcpErrorMessage without slicing. The same value is retained in the managed hover and included in the ARIA-label observable. The new dynamic list measures rows with offsetHeight. Upstream payloads are explicitly unbounded strings: Codex/Copilot pass SDK error strings directly, while extHostMcp.ts:655 builds a native connection error from await res.text(), which reads the entire HTTP response body. A misconfigured MCP URL can therefore place a large HTML/error response directly on this layout path.
Findings.Recommendation: Cap the inline/ARIA preview by bytes or lines before DOM assignment and constrain row height, while preserving access to the complete diagnostic through Show Output or an explicit on-demand expansion that performs the large layout only when requested.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The all-entry loop, per-label full snapshot construction, global event dependency, and synchronous measurement path are directly established. Only the exact duration for a user's installed-server count is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: UI-thread CPU, temporary server-presentation objects, and DOM height measurements
Findings.PerformanceScaling: With N installed host-backed servers, one customization event reads N labels; each label rebuilds and searches the N-server presentation snapshot, yielding O(N²) allocation/search work. The resulting rerender also invalidates N heights and measures visible rows. Startup/status bursts repeat the eager work; only the later animation-frame layout is coalesced.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased UI-thread latency, CPU/GC pressure, and potential dropped frames while the Customizations page is visible.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: ARIA observables were created and subscribed only when AccessibiltyRenderer rendered viewport rows, and status updates did not force a section-wide rerender.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A new section autorun reads every cached row label on any shared customization/session change, marks the whole list for remeasurement, and schedules rerender.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1747 newly executes label?.read(reader) for every section entry, converting viewport-limited label evaluation into all-entry work on each observed update.
Findings.Title: Avoid recomputing every server label on each update
Findings.Impact: With many installed MCP servers, startup, failure, recovery, or enablement updates can repeatedly delay interaction and rendering on the Customizations page.
Findings.Evidence: Lines 1746-1748 loop over every row label. getMcpEntryAriaLabel at lines 1785-1811 reads the global change signal and calls getMcpServers(...).find(...) for host rows. getMcpServers at agentHostCustomizationService.ts:232-255 flattens, filters, and maps the full snapshot per call. ListView.rerender at listView.ts:814-823 clears dynamic-height state for every item before visible-row offsetHeight probes. AccessibiltyRenderer at listWidget.ts:1313-1318 already subscribes rendered-row labels.
Findings.Recommendation: Leave label subscriptions with rendered accessibility rows. Use one shared status/session subscription to request layout, and invalidate only rows whose error text or visibility changed rather than eagerly evaluating all labels and rerendering the whole list.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the MCP Customizations home or installed-search results with many installed servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: List construction creates per-entry ARIA observables, then the new section autorun immediately evaluates all of them and schedules an animation-frame section layout before the list geometry settles.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: N installed rows; host-backed labels each reconstruct and search an N-server snapshot, so the new eager pass is O(N²). Only roughly the allocated viewport rows are synchronously height-probed, but rerender invalidates all N cached heights.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All observable evaluation and list measurement is serialized on the UI thread. MutableDisposable coalesces scheduled layouts to one per animation frame, but the eager all-label evaluation happens before scheduling and is not coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The WorkbenchList caches measured row heights, but the new rerender clears dynamic-height width validity for every item. getMcpServers has no presentation cache and rebuilds the flattened/mapped snapshot on every label evaluation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the all-entry autorun, full-snapshot materialization, and ListView rerender/offsetHeight path are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical installed MCP counts vary; the quadratic mechanism is certain, while noticeable jank is most likely for larger inventories or startup bursts.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated UI-thread work introduced by eagerly reading every row label and forcing section-wide remeasurement.

Scenarios.Scenario: A visible native or agent-host MCP server transitions to error, recovers, or changes its diagnostic
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The already-materialized status event synchronously updates row text/status and all subscribed ARIA labels; the section autorun then requests dynamic remeasurement and list layout on the next animation frame.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pre-existing notification per host state update; status transitions for multiple servers can arrive as a burst.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same snapshots were received, but ARIA computation remained viewport-scoped and did not force section-wide dynamic rerender.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The notification must arrive before the UI status event; the diff adds downstream all-row computation but does not add IPC.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N installed rows and E customization/native-state events. Host events incur O(E*N²) eager snapshot/search work; visible row measurement scales with viewport rows and wrapped diagnostic length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Status handlers run synchronously on the UI thread. Multiple layout requests within a frame are coalesced, but each event still performs the eager label loop, and visible dynamic measurement performs synchronous offsetHeight reads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache serves getMcpServers presentations. Dynamic row heights are cached between updates but are globally invalidated by rerender after each observed change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event propagation, eager computation, RAF scheduling, and synchronous list probing are established in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Status frequency depends on provider behavior and server count; repository comments/tests identify repeated error updates, while exact frame cost is environment-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable for the added all-row recomputation; ordinary single-row text updates alone would otherwise remain viewport-bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display a verbose MCP startup or connection error inline
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After an upstream failure supplies its message, the UI assigns the entire string to textContent, hover content, and an ARIA label, then browser wrapping and dynamic-height measurement must complete before the list geometry is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the complete failed HTTP/SSE response body with res.text() into the MCP connection error
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-body read per failed connection attempt; one resulting diagnostic is displayed per failed server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The body was already read and stored as an error message, but the Customizations row did not render or measure it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The pre-existing body read completes before the error state is published; the diff newly places the resulting unbounded string on the synchronous UI layout path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start a configured stdio MCP server and publish process startup/exit errors
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process launch per configured server start; failures publish one error state per failed attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subprocess errors produced compact status rows without inline full-message layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The pre-existing process failure precedes display; the diff only changes how the already-received message is rendered.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Raw error-message byte length and resulting wrapped line count; there is no length or line cap in the protocol, renderer, CSS, or dynamic row allocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM update, text wrapping, ARIA attribute update, and offsetHeight measurement are synchronous on the UI thread; width changes can repeat wrapping and measurement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The row skips rewriting unchanged text, but the complete payload remains retained in row/hover/accessibility state. Dynamic heights are invalidated on relevant updates and width changes; there is no bounded preview cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: raw upstream strings, full DOM assignment, no-clipping wrapping CSS, and synchronous dynamic measurement are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most errors are short, but a misconfigured HTTP endpoint can return a large HTML/error body and SDK error strings have no declared bound. Exact payload prevalence is uncertain; the unbounded layout mechanism is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable unbounded synchronous layout and retention; cap the inline preview while leaving full diagnostics available on demand.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize, scroll, collapse, or reopen a section containing dynamic error rows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ResizeObserver or section toggles schedule layout; WorkbenchList lays out the viewport and probes dynamic rows, preserving the scroll anchor. Scrolling materializes and measures newly visible error rows.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible dynamic rows, cached offscreen rows, container width changes, and each error's wrapped line count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resize callbacks are coalesced by the same next-animation-frame MutableDisposable. Measurement remains synchronous within that frame; no background worker or parallel boundary is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Measured heights are reused until rerender or width invalidation. The PR deliberately invalidates offscreen heights after status changes so later scrolling remeasures them.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: list dynamic-height implementation and resize/layout scheduling were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Normal short errors and the four-row minimum viewport keep ordinary resize cost bounded; very long errors are covered by the separate unbounded-payload finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: The dynamic-height mechanism is otherwise appropriately virtualized and frame-coalesced; no additional finding beyond all-row invalidation and unbounded payload size.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the More Actions menu and choose Show Output for an errored server
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click resolves the current row/session, builds menu actions, and invokes the existing native output or agent-host log handler only on explicit user action.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One action build and one output operation per user click; no loop over installed rows is introduced on this path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: User-triggered and serialized; there is no new fan-out, queue, or burst behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Actions retain DOM identity across message-only updates and resolve the current entry when invoked; no new cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: menu construction and both output routing branches were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Output-channel implementation cost was not material because invocation cardinality remains one per click and the diff moves, rather than multiplies, the existing operation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the boundary cardinality remains user-triggered and constant.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of all five changed files and all diff pages. Reported two introduced issues: section-wide quadratic label/snapshot recomputation with forced dynamic remeasurement, and unbounded inline layout of raw MCP error strings. Dynamic virtualization, resize coalescing, cleanup, output routing, tests, fixtures, and pre-existing IPC/network/subprocess boundaries were also inspected.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
